enforcedBy: the naming gate, which refuses the word in the concern slot because no declaration admits it

check.population: every filename that would carry the refused word, and the covering tags each refusal names
check.freshness: a verdict stands until a covering tag is renamed or removed, or the refused word is admitted by an approved edit
check.refusal: the lint run fails a filename carrying the refused word as its concern
check.observation: each refused word resolved through its covering-tag edges, which the resolution gate follows
check.evidence: fires-and-accepts: a suite lints a file whose concern slot holds an undeclared word and passes a file carrying a declared tag
check.authority: the covering tags, which a refused word resolves to, so admitting the word is an approved edit to the vocabulary

records.name: Spawner or Prefab as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file spawner or prefab, where the factory tag already covers a file that constructs instances.

records.name: Blueprint or Archetype as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file blueprint or archetype, where the specification tag covers a file that declares a rule and the template tag covers one that declares a shape.

records.name: Loop or Tick as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a simulation's main loop or its tick as its own concern, where the engine tag covers the file that runs the loop and the step tag covers one advance.

records.name: Batcher as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file batcher, where the batching tag already covers a file that groups small operations into larger ones.

records.name: Spatial Index as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a spatial hash or a quadtree as a domain concern, where a lookup structure over known members takes the registry tag.

records.name: Keybinding as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file keybinding or control-scheme, where the binding tag already covers a file that ties a name to what it resolves to.

records.name: Control Widget as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a slider or a toggle control by its kind of control, where the widget tag covers every interactive control.

records.name: Condition as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file condition or phase-condition, where the predicate tag already covers a file that answers yes or no.

records.name: Strategy as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file strategy or difficulty-policy, where the policy tag already covers a file that chooses among behaviors by a rule.

records.name: Agent Memory as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file pattern-memory or agent-memory, where the memory tag already covers what an agent remembers between steps.

records.name: Savegame as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file savegame or autosave, where the persistence tag covers saving state and the store tag covers holding it.

records.name: Pause or Boot as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file after one lifecycle moment such as pause, boot or teardown, where the lifecycle tag covers how a component starts and stops.

records.name: Screen or Page as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file endscreen, hud-panel or page, where the view tag covers a file that renders one screen.

records.name: Page Script as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file page-script, where the entrypoint tag covers the file a runtime starts from.

records.name: Preloader as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file preloader or asset-loader, where the loader tag already covers reading a resource into memory.

records.name: Object Pool as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file object-pool, where the pool tag already covers keeping reusable instances.

records.name: Cooldown as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file cooldown or throttle, where the throttling tag covers limiting how often something runs and the timer tag covers running it after a delay.

records.name: Thread as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file thread, where the worker tag covers running work apart from the caller.

records.name: Particle Emitter as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file particle-emitter, where the emitter tag already covers a file that produces output for others to receive.

records.name: Juice or Screenshake as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file feedback, juice or screenshake, where the effect tag covers feedback that leaves the state behind it unchanged.

records.name: Manager as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file manager, which names a stature rather than a role, where the coordinator tag covers a file that owns a lifecycle and the service tag one that offers a stateful capability.

records.name: Page Feature as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file page-feature or plug-in behavior, where the extension and plugin tags cover capability added to a host.

records.name: Id Table as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file ids, id-table or symbol-table, where the constants collection tag covers a file of fixed named values.

records.name: Attack Pattern as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file weapon-pattern or attack-pattern, where the behavior tag covers a file that decides and the specification tag one that only declares.

records.name: Checker or Linter as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file checker or linter, where the validator tag covers a file that decides whether its input is valid.

records.name: Scanner as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file scanner, which overlaps reporter and inspector, where the analyzer and inspector tags cover a file that reads material and derives facts from it.

records.name: Fixer or Healer as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file fixer, healer or repairer, where the transformer tag covers a file that maps an input state to an output state.

records.name: Walker or Crawler as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file walker or crawler, where the iterator tag covers a file that yields the members of a set.

records.name: Gate as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file gate, which names a decision rather than a thing, where the predicate and validator tags cover the decision it makes.

records.name: Index as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file index, which overlaps cache and registry, where the registry tag covers a lookup over known members.

records.name: Handler as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file handler, which fits every role, where the processor tag covers applying an operation to each item and the coordinator tag covers driving collaborators.

records.name: Guide or Note as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file doc, guide or note, where the reference tag covers authored knowledge a reader consults.

records.name: Plan as a Tag
records.definition: Tagging a file plan, where the specification tag covers a file that declares a required end state.
